title: Trendlines and channels
desc: Draw a line under the lows, add a channel, and read a break

cards.title: The line breaks
cards.situation: You drew a trendline under three rising lows. Today price closed just below it. What does that tell you?

chart.label: A rising trendline under three lows; today price closes just below it

options.text: The uptrend is over: sell everything
options.feedback: A break is a warning, not a signal. Price often dips under a line and climbs back.

options.text: A warning: watch for lower highs and lows
options.feedback: The break says the trend is weakening. The next highs and lows tell you if it’s really over.
A break does matter: buyers didn’t defend the line this time. Treat it as a warning and watch the next swings.

cards.work: Line at $47.80 today, close $47.20: about 1% below. One close isn’t a new trend.

cards.title: Draw it under the lows
cards.text: In an uptrend, connect **at least two rising lows** with a straight line and extend it to the right. In a downtrend, connect the falling highs.

chart.label: An uptrend line drawn under three rising lows

blocks.tip: Two lows make a line. Each extra touch makes it more worth watching.

cards.title: Add a second line: a channel
cards.text: Draw a parallel line through the highs. Price often travels between the two, like a lane.

visual.title: Daily · rising channel

chart.label: A rising channel: a lower line under the lows, drag the upper line onto the highs

visual.label: upper line
visual.done: That’s a channel: price travels between the two lines.

cards.foot: Near the lower line, buyers often step in. Near the upper line, sellers do. Treat both as zones, not exact prices.

cards.title: Don’t bend the line to fit
cards.text: If the line cuts through candles, or you redraw it every day to make it work, it isn’t a trendline. It’s a wish.

chart.label: A dashed line forced through the candle bodies

cards.rule: use clear swing lows, the same way every time. No forcing.

cards.title: How many lows?
cards.q: What’s the fewest swing lows you need to draw an uptrend line?

chart.label: A rising chart with no line drawn yet

options.feedback: One low can’t set a direction: any line passes through a single point. A second rising low fixes the slope.
Two rising lows fix the line. Each extra touch makes it more worth watching, but two are enough to draw it.
Two lows are enough to draw a line. A third touch makes it more trustworthy, but it isn’t needed to draw it.
You never need that many. Two lows are enough to draw it; extra touches only add trust.

cards.title: At the top line
cards.q: A stock moves in a rising channel. It’s touching the upper line again. What often happens there?

options.text: It breaks out higher every time
options.feedback: The upper line works like a ceiling. Price often pulls back toward the lower line, though sometimes it breaks out.

options.text: Sellers often step in and price pulls back
options.feedback: Near the upper line, sellers often step in. Price tends to pull back toward the lower line, though sometimes it breaks out.

options.text: The uptrend is over for good
options.feedback: A touch of the upper line is the channel doing its job. Nothing has broken; sellers just often step in there.
Touching the upper line is the channel working. It counts until price clearly breaks out of it.

cards.headline: You can draw a trend, not just see it.
lines: Uptrend line: under at least two rising lows.
A channel adds a parallel line through the highs.
A break is a warning, not a signal.
